description: Reduce block2 width from 256 to 192 (widths 64/192/256) to cut conv FLOPs.
Use a constant Muon norm_freq of 8 instead of the 2-to-17 schedule, which cuts the number of norm computations.
Train on bilinearly downscaled 28x28 images for the first half of steps, then switch to full 32x32, with automatic dynamic shapes disabled so each size compiles statically.
The Muon helper was recompiled every step because the Python int step count is specialised by torch.compile, so I now pass the step as a CUDA tensor and raised the dynamo cache limit as a safeguard.
The Muon helper was recompiled every step because the Python int step count is specialised by torch.compile, so I now pass the step as a CUDA tensor and raised the dynamo cache limit as a safeguard.
Cut EPOCHS from 7.65 to 7.04 (92%) so every schedule, including the LR decay to zero, ends 8% earlier and training stops there.
Use only the original and flipped views (2 instead of 6) for TTA on the 25% least confident test images to cut predict time.

issues: No integrity problems found. The diff only removes one Newton-Schulz iteration from the Muon orthogonalisation step. It carries nothing between runs, adds no seeding, does not touch the test images, adds no file access and adds no imports.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. With one fewer iteration the update is less orthogonalised, which is a legitimate speed-for-accuracy tradeoff. The loop and transpose logic stay consistent.

The provisional reject decision fits the numbers. The candidate's adjusted cost is 0.4014 and the incumbent's mean is -0.0543, so the candidate is about 0.456 worse. That is far more than the job noise sd of 0.026, so the faster step does not make up for the accuracy loss.

Recomputed z: 0.4557 / (0.026 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) gives about -14.31, using the sign convention where negative means the candidate is worse. The harness reports -14.425. The small gap probably comes from the harness using an estimated sd (about 0.0258) instead of 0.026. Either value supports a clear rejection.
The evidence is thin: there is only 1 candidate run and 2 incumbent runs. The gap is large enough that this does not change the decision.

description: Remove the third unrolled Newton-Schulz iteration in the Muon helper, keeping 2 NS steps to save optimizer time.
Use 480 instead of 960 training images for whitening initialisation to reduce setup time.
Switch compile mode from max-autotune to max-autotune-no-cudagraphs for forward_step and the model to check whether cudagraph overhead affects run time.
Halve WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 0.1 so the whitening bias stops training sooner.
Change widths to block1=48, block2=256, block3=320 to cut full-resolution conv cost and add capacity in the 4x4 stage.
Replace SiLU with GELU in ConvGroup activations to test whether a cheaper fused kernel lowers run time at similar accuracy.
Disable color jitter augmentation in train() by setting its enabled flag to False.
Train the first third of steps on 24x24 images, downscaled once per epoch in the loader, with an adaptive final max pool so the network works at both resolutions.

issues: No integrity issues: no seeding, file access, test-image use or state carried between runs. resize starts as None in each new loader and is set inside the timed train().
The untimed first call compiles both the 24 px and 32 px shapes. That is allowed compile-only carry-over, and the incumbent already switched shapes (28 px, then 32 px) the same way.
MaxPool2d(3) -> AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) is correct and needed: a 24 px input leaves a 2x2 final map, and at 32 px (3x3 map) both layers give the same output.
The switch to 32 px is checked once per epoch, at the start, so the 1/3 boundary is rounded to whole epochs. This only affects exact timing.

Recomputed z: candidate mean -0.09245 vs incumbent -0.0543, gain 0.03815; with sd 0.026 per job and n=2 on each side, SE = 0.026, so z ~ 1.467. The harness reports 1.480; the small gap probably comes from a slightly different sd estimate. The provisional reject (below threshold) is consistent.

description: Train the first third of steps on 24x24 images, downscaled once per epoch in the loader, with an adaptive final max pool so the network works at both resolutions.
Skip the random pre-flip pass (batch_flip_lr) at epoch 0 so only the deterministic every-other-epoch flip remains.
Change the BatchNorm default momentum argument from 0.5566 to 0.45, so the torch running-stat momentum becomes 0.55.
For the first 30% of steps feed 28x28 center-cropped inputs (no interpolation) instead of the bilinear 28x28 downscale for the first half.
Apply a power of 1.3 to the linear LR decay factors for both the whiten bias and the other optimizers, so the LR still ends at zero.
